notes: One autumn cohort, two price registers, two dead press files. Last year's A4-landscape COMMUNITY completion certificate converts cleanly and DOES carry a seal graphic frame, but its letterspaced credential-number run is dropped from the mapping readout while its line break is kept, so every offset past it runs short and the trailing HONOURS field goes silently absent (validator says VALID, prepare says success). The 2019 EXECUTIVE diploma was built by a different shop as one continuous typeset block, so it converts to a SINGLE text frame holding every line and ZERO graphic frames — no target to bind a per-record seal, every field driven by offset arithmetic. A 30-row registrar export whose tier lives ONLY inside the programme code (CPE = community, CXP = executive), with one un-removed week-3 withdrawal (blank completion + blank credential), an adjacent duplicate credential number (CL-2026-0119 on two people), diacritics that mostly use precomposed accents but on two names slip into an ASCII digraph/stripped convention (Bjoern for Bjoern/Bjorn, Muller for the umlaut name), and an honours column blank for the ENTIRE community register even though the community face carries an honours line. A colourless raking-light seal impression whose right side sits at cream luminance so an arc of the rope border and part of '1978' silently drop from any selection. Six staff phone frames of the hall and two buildings: three carry an HDR-lifted milky black point that only greys next to the clean three, and one hall interior sits a degree off level with almost no spare margin so straightening eats the cover crop. Plus Helen Abbott's clean registrar note (two programmes, code convention, who signs what, sponsor complaint, executive honours grades).

LAYOUT SPEC for last year's community completion certificate press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single certificate, A4 LANDSCAPE (297 x 210 mm), fonts embedded, produced from a real InDesign page layout so it converts cleanly to a native .indd. This is the file the closed shop printed the community certificates from.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (community Certificate of Completion):
- Ground: Warm Certificate Cream #F3EBD8 across the full page.
- Top: 'CEDARLINE INSTITUTE' in small-caps, Cedar Green #33503C, a warm legible serif; a thin Engraved Gold #9A7B33 rule beneath.
- Heading: 'Certificate of Completion' centred, Deep Ink #1E2620.
- 'This certifies that' (static, small).
- RECIPIENT NAME - large, centred, Deep Ink #1E2620.
- 'has completed the Certificate in' (static) then the PROGRAMME TITLE.
- COMPLETION DATE line.
- A small LETTERSPACED CREDENTIAL NUMBER, e.g. 'No. CL-2026-0101', Slate Grey #5A6066, set with wide letter-spacing (tracking).
- A small HONOURS line beneath the credential number.
- A blind-emboss SEAL position at lower-centre-left (a real graphic frame).
- Two signature lines at the foot: 'Helen Abbott - Registrar' and 'Callum Reyes - Community Programme Lead'.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The RECIPIENT NAME, the PROGRAMME TITLE, the COMPLETION DATE, the letterspaced CREDENTIAL NUMBER and the HONOURS line are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing down the centre, NOT five addressable frames; each is its own paragraph/run inside that one story.
- The two SIGNATORY lines sit alone in their own separate frame at the foot of the page.
- There IS a real rectangular GRAPHIC FRAME at the seal position - so this file, unlike the executive one, gives a per-record seal a target to bind into.
- THE OFFSET / OMISSION TRAP: the credential number is set as its own run with wide letter-spacing (tracking) inside the flowing story. The convenience mapping readout (generate_indd_mapping_prompt / the textContent readback) OMITS that letterspaced run's characters while KEEPING its line break, so the reconstructed string still looks well formed and validates VALID, but every character offset past that point is short by the length of the credential-number run. prepare_indd_merge_template reports success, and the field that follows in the flow - the HONOURS line - ends up silently absent from the prepared template. The true story must be rebuilt by concatenating the content runs from the exported IDML and every offset computed from that string, not from the readout.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): RECIPIENT_NAME | PROGRAMME_TITLE | COMPLETION_DATE | CREDENTIAL_NUMBER | HONOURS. (The two signatory lines are static.)

Colours: Warm Certificate Cream #F3EBD8 ground, Cedar Green #33503C institute name, Deep Ink #1E2620 name and heading, Slate Grey #5A6066 letterspaced credential number, Engraved Gold #9A7B33 heading rule.

assets.defect_engineered: EXECUTIVE press file built as one continuous typeset block: converts to a SINGLE text frame holding every line and ZERO graphic frames, so there is no target to bind a per-record seal and all fields must be driven by offset arithmetic inside one story (this IS the checkpoint-after-step-9 architecture trap; invisible until converted and the IDML is read).
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the 2019 executive diploma press PDF (flat, single record; unchanged since 2019; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single diploma, LANDSCAPE, larger and more formal than the community certificate (approx. A3 landscape, 420 x 297 mm), generous margins, fonts embedded, produced in 2019 by a DIFFERENT print shop than the community file. Converts to a native .indd.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (executive Diploma):
- Ground: Warm Certificate Cream #F3EBD8, framed by a double Engraved Gold #9A7B33 rule with wide margins.
- 'CEDARLINE INSTITUTE' engraved at the top in a high-contrast serif, Cedar Green #33503C.
- Formal centred prose across several typeset lines: 'This is to certify that [NAME] has satisfied the requirements of the Executive Programme in Professional Practice, completed on [DATE], and is hereby awarded this Diploma [HONOURS]. Credential [CREDENTIAL NUMBER].'
- A blind-emboss SEAL sits at the foot centre of the printed page.
- Two signature lines: 'Dr Miriam Voss - Director of Executive Education' and 'Helen Abbott - Registrar'.
- It reads as the more carefully made of the two documents - heavier, engraved, restrained.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the trap - invisible until converted and the IDML is read):
- The WHOLE face is one continuous typeset block. The conversion yields a SINGLE text frame holding EVERY line - heading, body prose, name, programme, date, honours, credential number and both signatory names - as ONE story. There are no per-field frames.
- There is NO graphic frame anywhere on the page. The seal that reads on the printed diploma was flattened into the artwork / set as an inline element, so after conversion there is NO picture or graphic frame to bind a per-record seal into.
- Consequently every variable field must be driven by OFFSET ARITHMETIC computed inside that one story, and a per-record seal cannot be placed through the merge into this file at all. This forces the executive-register architecture decision: drive its fields by offsets, and decide whether the seal can be placed by another route or whether the executive register must ride a community-derived template at a corrected (heavier) type register - weighing what a 9,000-dollar credential loses either way against the registrar's fear of looking like a printable freebie.
- The printed diploma says none of this; it is the more polished-looking of the two files.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): NAME | PROGRAMME_TITLE | COMPLETION_DATE | CREDENTIAL_NUMBER | HONOURS.

Colours: Warm Certificate Cream #F3EBD8 ground, Deep Ink #1E2620 body, Engraved Gold #9A7B33 double rule and flourishes, Cedar Green #33503C institute name.

assets.defect_engineered: Colourless blind-emboss photographed in raking light from the left: relief and cream stock are the same warm cream, so the seal reads only as shadow. Along the RIGHT side of the ring the light falls away and relief and stock sit at the same luminance, so a selection has nothing to hold and silently loses an arc of the rope border and part of the founding year 1978 - the mask still looks like a seal and the trace still succeeds. Fires checkpoint-after-step-6.
assets.prompt: Extreme close-up photograph, low raking side light coming from the LEFT, of a blind-embossed institutional seal pressed into cream-coloured certificate paper stock. The seal is COLOURLESS - there is no ink, only relief pressed into the paper, so the entire seal is the same warm cream as the paper around it and reads only as soft shadow and highlight thrown by the low-angle light. The seal is a circular medallion: an outer ROPE BORDER of twisted-rope relief; inside it the small-caps words CEDARLINE INSTITUTE curving around the top of the ring; the founding year 1 9 7 8 curving across the bottom of the ring; and a stylised single CEDAR TREE device embossed in the centre. Because the light rakes from the left, the left and top of the rope ring catch a crisp bright highlight and a dark shadow edge and read clearly, but along the RIGHT SIDE of the ring the light falls away and the embossed relief and the flat cream stock sit at almost exactly the same luminance, so the rope border and the year digits on the lower right lose nearly all their shadow and very nearly vanish into the cream. Fine paper grain, subtle fibre texture, no colour anywhere, warm neutral cream throughout, realistic photograph of an embossed certificate under grazing light, shallow relief.

assets.content:
CEDARLINE INSTITUTE - autumn cohort, note from the Registrar's office (Helen Abbott)

For whoever is setting the credentials this year. Read this before you touch the export.

THE TWO PROGRAMMES
We run one subject, Professional Practice, at two very different registers, and they must never come off the press looking like the same document.
- The Community Evening Programme. A hundred and eighty dollars, one evening a week, mostly younger working adults. The credential is a Certificate of Completion. It is a warm, plain, honest thing and it goes on a kitchen wall. In the export these carry a programme code beginning CPE.
- The Executive Programme. Nine thousand dollars, bought by the candidate's employer, and the diploma ends up framed in an office where that person's own clients read it. It is a Diploma, heavier and more formal, and it is the one the sponsoring firms judge us by. In the export these carry a programme code beginning CXP.
There is no separate column that tells you which is which. The code is the only place it lives, so split the cohort off the code and nothing else.

WHO SIGNS WHAT
- Community certificate: two signatures - Helen Abbott, Registrar, and Callum Reyes, Community Programme Lead.
- Executive diploma: two signatures - Dr Miriam Voss, Director of Executive Education, and Helen Abbott, Registrar.
The signature lines are already on both old press files. Do not move them.

HONOURS
The executive diploma carries an honours line: With Distinction, With Merit, or Pass, and the grade is in the export for those candidates. Set it exactly as recorded.

NAMES
Every name is set the way that candidate spells it, accents and all. We have had complaints from graduates whose names were flattened. If a name looks as though an accent has been dropped or spelled around, ask me before you print it - do not guess.

THE SPONSORS
Two autumn cohorts ago a sponsoring firm told us the executive diploma looked like something printed off a website. That is the single thing we cannot repeat. If the executive credential reads like the evening certificate in a frame, we will hear about it within the week.

THE SEAL
The seal is ours - it is the Institute's own device, the cedar and the founding year, 1978. It is not to be reinvented or redrawn from imagination. Whatever seal ends up on these credentials has to be our seal, the same one pressed into the certificate on the wall of the hall.

CORRECTIONS
Names get corrected right up to the morning of the ceremony. Whatever the programme and the card are built in, I have to be able to open them and fix a spelling myself an hour before we start.

Learning that holds up. - H.A.
